posts.name: 37-world-ancient-cannabis
posts.caption:
Scientists say hair from a 2,800 year old Siberian royal tomb holds traces of cannabis, the earliest direct evidence of people using it as a drug 🌿

The grave in Tyva also held about 1,000 cannabis seeds and many sacrificed horses. The authors even suggest the plant may have calmed people chosen for sacrifice, but that is a hypothesis. An outside forensic toxicologist says the hair test is weak, because hair buried next to cannabis could absorb traces without anyone using it.

Source: Caspari et al. (University of Bern, Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology), “Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2,800 years ago”, Science, 2026.
